notes:
Lead background: small SaaS (support automation) replacing legacy rule engine with LLM-driven assistants. Ran quick POC with hosted API. Primary goal: stable streaming + tool-calls so agents can call internal ticketing APIs via function schemas.

Problem summary: intermittent JSON parse failures when consuming streaming responses in JSON mode / function-calling flows. Reported symptoms: partial chunks that are not valid JSON until stream end; sometimes model emits explanatory text before the JSON object; occasionally schema fields are strings instead of nested objects (e.g. 'actions' returned as stringified JSON). Customer client is strict JSON parser (golang stdlib) — fails fast.

Tech notes captured in call:
- They are using streaming + function-calling and expecting each finished function call to be a single JSON object that can be unmarshaled as it arrives.
- Observed behavior: server emits delta events (chunks) where the json object assembles over time; client tries to parse on first closing brace and fails when trailing tokens arrive out of expected order.
- Other gotchas: trailing commas in model-generated arrays (rare), and model sometimes adds human commentary before the function payload when instruction prompt includes examples.

What customer tried: local buffering and naive concatenation — reduced failures but still edge cases. They attempted regex post-processing (dangerous). They reached out to ask if Redwood has recommended pattern for streaming + function schema enforcement.

Quote from customer: 'We need the assistant to trigger ticket.create with a strict payload — if the schema isn't exact our downstream API rejects it and users see failures.'

Potential risks: if not resolved, customer may pause rollout and evaluate other providers (OpenAI mentioned). Cost sensitivity: SMB — expects low run costs; prefers hosted API with predictable usage and simple integration.

Suggested actions (internal):
- SE deep-dive to walk through stream sample and show robust client patterns (buffer until final event/stream end, use content-disposition markers, or rely on non-streaming function call mode for strict handshake).
- Provide example code (Go/Node) that collects streaming chunks and validates JSON schema only after stream completion; include defensive parsing snippets (stream-safe JSON builder).
- Proposal: short-term workaround doc + code sample by 2026-03-13; longer-term: escalate to eng if we see model emitting non-JSON tokens consistently (ticket INF-3241).

Next steps with customer: schedule 60m technical session w/ Priya, provide sample code, request sign-off on security checklist.
